children: Norway’s current account recorded a surplus of NOK 279 billion in the second quarter of 2026, marking the largest surplus since the first quarter of 2023 and widening from NOK 185 billion in the corresponding period of the previous year.

The increase was largely driven by a bigger surplus in the goods account, which expanded to NOK 242.5 billion from NOK 149 billion, while the services account deficit narrowed to NOK 10.3 billion from NOK 17.7 billion.
At the same time, the shortfall in current transfers (secondary income) declined to NOK 12.5 billion from NOK 20.4 billion.
On the other hand, surplus in the compensation of employees and investment income (primary income) decreased to NOK 59.3 billion from NOK 74.1 billion a year ago.

title: Norway Current Account Surplus Largest in Over 3 Years
